## Biography
### Early Life
Stephanie Nilles was born in Chicago, Illinois, and grew up in its suburbs. She began studying piano and cello at six. Her childhood teachers included pianist Annie Marchand Sherter and cellist Tanya Lesinsky Carey. She earned a Bachelor of Music in classical piano performance at the Cleveland Institute of Music, studying with Olga Radosavljevich and Anita Pontremoli. Her early achievements included a Fischoff Competition gold medal.[[1]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-1)[[2]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-2) Her younger brother’s participation in a jazz orchestra introduced her to Charles Mingus through “Jump Monk.”[[3]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-3)

## Biography
### Career
Nilles moved to New York in 2006, began writing music, and worked as an administrative and research assistant at Yeshiva University’s Center for Ethics. She performed in the East Village anti-folk scene and subsequently developed an international touring career, including a substantial association with New Orleans. She also sang with Bobby McFerrin at Carnegie Hall.[[2]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-2)[[1]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-1) Her recordings include the 2013 collaboration ...Takes a Big Ship with Zach Brock& the Magic Number and the 2015 album Uncle Stephanie’s Murder Ballads *FOR KIDS!, featuring bassist Jesse Morrow and drummer Paul Thibodeaux.[[4]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-4)[[5]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-5)
Sunnyside released I pledge allegiance to the flag - the white flag in March 2021. Recorded in Bremen in December 2019, it presents her solo interpretations of Charles Mingus, closing with John Coltrane’s “Alabama.”[[3]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-3) She also composed and performed music for NDR’s eight-part adaptation of John Steinbeck’s Jenseits von Eden, broadcast in 2021, with instrumental contributions from Thomas Deakin and Allan Nilles.[[6]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-6)

## Biography
### Musical Style
Nilles combines classical piano technique with jazz, blues, boogie-woogie, anti-folk, and a confrontational cabaret sensibility. Her performances juxtapose rough vocal delivery, rhythmic drive, humor, and socially critical songwriting. Reviews of ...Takes a Big Ship describe honky-tonk textures, prepared piano, and abrupt changes between exuberant ensemble playing and ballads.[[4]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-4) Although piano and voice are central, her recording credits also include organ, electric autoharp, percussion, melodica, and violin.[[5]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-5)[[6]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-6)

## Biography
### Legacy
Nilles’s documented recognition spans jazz interpretation and dramatic composition. The New York City Jazz Record included I pledge allegiance to the flag - the white flag in its Best of 2021 selections for albums, tributes, and solo recordings. These were year-end editorial selections rather than a single competitive Album of the Year award.[[7]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-7) Jenseits von Eden, featuring her original score, received the 2022 German Audiobook Prize for Best Radio Play.[[6]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-6)

## Fun Facts
*   Her venue biography reports three NPR appearances by age seventeen.[[1]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-1)  
*   She and Thomas Deakin met at a music and circus guild festival in 2015.[[8]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-8)  
*   Her murder-ballads album credits her with electric autoharp and drummer Paul Thibodeaux with a bucket of rocks.[[5]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-5)  
*   She recorded her Mingus tribute at Bremen’s Sendesaal, where Mingus had performed decades earlier; most selections were captured in first or second takes.[[3]](https://jazzapedia.com/artists/stephanie-nilles#ref-3)

## Musical Connections
### Influences
*   Charles Mingus - A formative jazz discovery whose compositions entered her repertoire in 2007 and became the focus of her solo tribute. (I pledge allegiance to the flag - the white flag) [2007–2021]  
*   Christian Howes - Sunnyside’s notes identify the violinist as an important mentor who helped her move from classical training toward jazz improvisation.

## Musical Connections
### Collaborators
*   Zach Brock - Co-billed violinist on their collaborative album; he also contributed violin and effects to her subsequent murder-ballads recording. (...Takes a Big Ship; Uncle Stephanie's Murder Ballads *FOR KIDS!) [2013–2015]  
*   Thomas Deakin - Began performing with Nilles after meeting in 2015. He also played multiple instruments and sang on her score for NDR’s East of Eden adaptation. [2015–2021]  
*   Bobby McFerrin - Nilles sang with McFerrin at Carnegie Hall, an appearance documented in her venue biography.

## Musical Connections
### Bandmates
*   Jesse Morrow - Played bass in her New Orleans quartet and is credited on her murder-ballads album. (Uncle Stephanie's Murder Ballads *FOR KIDS!)

## Musical Connections
### Teachers
*   Annie Marchand Sherter - Taught Nilles piano while she was growing up in suburban Chicago, according to Sunnyside’s biography.  
*   Tanya Lesinsky Carey - Taught Nilles cello during her upbringing in suburban Chicago.  
*   Olga Radosavljevich - One of Nilles’s teachers during her classical piano studies at the Cleveland Institute of Music.  
*   Anita Pontremoli - Taught Nilles at the Cleveland Institute of Music, where she earned her piano-performance degree.
